From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: support@pacificpharm.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional request reroute & SLA impact — PacificPharm

Hi Elena,

Quick note to let you know we detected an elevated error rate and p95 latency spike for requests from your primary region (us-west-1) starting ~07:58 PDT. Traffic for a subset of requests was automatically rerouted to our fallback pool in us-east while we engaged the autoscaling and routing playbooks.

Impact we observed: about 12% of API calls returned 5xx or timed out for ~18 minutes, and p95 for generation increased from ~420ms to ~1.6s for routed requests. We understand this can affect your latency SLAs for synchronous inference.

What we did immediately:
- Triggered emergency autoscale for us-west pool
- Enabled a temporary routing cap to preserve steady throughput (this routed ~30% of new sessions to us-east)
- Escalated to SRE to investigate root cause (KV eviction pressure on us-west cache nodes)

Next steps we are executing now:
- Roll back the routing cap if autoscale stabilizes (expected within 30–45m)
- Provide a post-incident timeline and metrics export once we complete analysis

I’m looping in support@pacificpharm.com so your engineering ops team sees live updates. I’ll follow up with a brief after we have the timeline and remediation items.

Sincere apologies for the disruption — we know latency is critical for your pipelines.

Best,
Rafael
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Rafael — SRE update: we identified aggressive KV eviction cycles on the us-west metadata nodes caused by a rare workload with large ephemeral key churn. Autoscale added serving instances but the metadata layer required a controlled restart to release fragmented memory.

Actions taken at 08:22:
- Drained two metadata replicas and restarted the cache process (expected catch-up within 3–5 minutes)
- Throttled background compaction and increased cache TTL for session keys for the affected tenant(s)
- Coordinated temporary routing cap (already applied) to limit fanout to us-east and reduce pressure

Short-term ETA: 20–30m for full stabilization. No evidence of truncated content from the runtime — errors were 5xx gateway/timeouts, not partial tokens. Marcus will validate logs for any truncation at the generation layer.

Sergio
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Update: stabilization in us-west & next steps — PacificPharm

Elena/Brian — quick update following SRE remediation.

Summary: us-west metadata replicas were restarted and the working set pressure has reduced. We observed the error rate drop back below baseline at ~08:50 PDT. We removed the temporary routing cap at 09:00 and began gradual re-homing of sessions to us-west.

Customer-visible notes:
- During the event (~07:58–08:50) roughly 12% of API calls for your tenant returned 5xx or timed out; about 30% of new sessions were routed to us-east with an elevated p95 (~1.6s) for those routed requests.
- We do not see evidence of truncated or partial generations; errors were surfaced as timeouts/502s rather than partial content.

Follow-ups we are providing:
1) Full incident timeline and metric snapshot (attached)
2) Root-cause analysis and remediation plan (we will send a short RCA by Monday)
3) If you prefer, we can open a dedicated review call with our SRE/infra team to walk through the timeline — happy to schedule.

Apologies again for the disruption. If this caused downstream work throttles or SLA impact, we will include this in the RCA and commercial review.

Best,

Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — PacificPharm (RCA forthcoming)

Elena/Brian — thanks again for your patience. This is a short post-incident summary while we finish the full RCA.

What happened (short):
- On 2026-08-07 07:58 PDT, a tenant-driven spike in ephemeral key churn caused metadata cache fragmentation in us-west, leading to increased eviction cycles and elevated latency.
- Our autoscaling mitigations added serving capacity but metadata fragmentation required a controlled restart to recover.

Customer impact:
- Window: 07:58–08:50 PDT
- Error rate: peak ~12% of API calls returning 5xx/timeouts for PacificPharm tenant
- Routing: ~30% of new sessions rerouted to us-east for a short window; routed requests had p95 ~1.6s vs baseline ~420ms
- No instances of truncated generation or partial tokens observed in sampled logs

What we changed (remediation):
- SRE: introduced a graceful cache defragmentation process to reduce need for restarts
- Runtime: temporary guardrails to limit per-tenant ephemeral key churn under high write patterns
- Orchestration: updated routing policy threshold to prefer local rehome only after metadata layer signals healthy

Planned follow-ups:
- Full RCA with timeline and specific telemetry (target Monday EOD)
- Joint review call if helpful (let us know availability)
- Commercial review if you would like to discuss SLA credit (Lauren will reach out only if requested)

Attachments: incident_timeline_pacificpharm_20260807.pdf (includes minute-by-minute traces), metrics_snapshot_us-west.csv

If you have any remaining questions or want the logs for a specific time slice, tell us which span and we’ll export it.

Regards,
